I cannot thank West Loop Veterinary Care in Chicago enough for the outstanding service they provided. I urgently needed a USDA certificate for my dog in order to travel internationally, and the clinic truly came to the rescue. This clinic goes above and beyond in every sense — professionalism, expertise, and genuine care for their clients and pets. I wholeheartedly recommend West Loop Veterinary Care to anyone in need of veterinary services. They are truly the highest standard of excellence.

***UPDATE: I was initially told the exam fee could be waived, but that offer was reversed after the owner, Dr. Solomon, declined to approve it. Choosing revenue over timely comfort for pets with a well-documented chronic history is unacceptable and speaks volumes about how clients are treated.***

I’ve been coming here for years and in the past this clinic felt like a true neighborhood, family style vet. Unfortunately, that has changed.

I recently requested a simple prescription refill for an ear ointment my dogs have been on for three to four years for routine maintenance. Despite the fact that my dogs had their annual exam and were seen in July 2025, well within the 12 month window, Dr. Behnke refused to refill the prescription without another exam.

I explained that this is not a new medication and that I cannot justify an additional $200 exam fee solely to refill a long standing prescription. I was told that if their ears were getting bad, I should bring them in, which would result in the additional charges on top of the medication.

What was most frustrating was the lack of consideration for my dogs’ comfort over the weekend. This is an ointment that has been prescribed many times before, not a new or controlled medication.

It’s disappointing that a situation as simple as a routine prescription refill is what will likely end a long term relationship with a veterinarian I once trusted.

Thank you for your help and the care that you gave Mouse.

Every single person we encountered was compassionate and genuinely cared about our cat Augie and us. Everything was thoroughly explained, we were offered multiple treatment options and there was never any judgement, just kindness and patience.
Augie had to stay two nights and we were encouraged to stay with him whenever we were able. The three nurses who cared for him, all truly made the experience so much easier. I feel awful that I cannot remember everyone's name because I was so upset, but the nurse the first night monitored him so carefully while he was sedated, distracted us with stories and funny conversation, and moved Augie to a more isolated space after his procedure because he is so afraid of any noise. If we ever have another urgent situation, with any of our kitties in the future, we would not even consider going anywhere but here! I will be forever grateful for the quality of the care we received, and the kindness of the entire staff.

Wow! I'm sitting next to a very content cat right now, all rolled up into a ball. I think he was happier today than your average day, and had some excitement. This is a cat that went to the vet today.

A little backstory, my little guy, whom is a kitten, has only been to VetCo (PetCo's mobile veterinarian service) and PAWS, for vaccines and neutering. VetCo has been such a horrible experience, that little my cat is traumatized by this point, from seeing a vet. They couldn't even complete his pre-surgical examination at PAWS, by the time I took him there just 12 days ago, because he was so freaked out (and he isn't really a little scaredy cat, nor is he fractious at home).

So finally, I got him into VCA for his first real vet appointment. I didn't expect for them to be able to examine him, but at least I knew I could get all my health questions for him answered, and hopefully they wouldn't tell me to never to bring him back again.

I forgot to ask if they had cat empathetic or Fear-Free certified veterinarians there, when making an appointment, so I asked when I arrived. The front desk staff didn't know what I was talking about, but started listing amongst themselves some of their vets that were already really good with cats, and one of them just happened to be who my baby got to see today.

The front desk staff were super attentive to my furball's needs and friendly throughout the visit. They got me out of the stress of the front waiting area with the other animals, and into a exam room right away.

They let me take him out of his carrier, but we hardly had to wait at all, despite being early for the appointment. I brought toys and treats, and put him on the metal exam table, so I could start helping him make a positive association with those tables. When the veterinarian came in, he was so cool!

I got to asking my questions first, and by the time I was done, FluffBall wasn't even afraid of the vet anymore- just a little timid. And BAM! We got a whole physical examination done! No hissing, not a thing! The veterinarian even checked his mouth, and my little guy was cooler with it than he is with me doing that!

MIND YOU, this was a previously "fractious" cat, that was at the point before this that he could barely be touched by a vet or their technician. A miracle!

Not only that, but my little guy got a welcome bag! It had toys and all sorts of goodies in it, and he was so excited to get it! VCA is running first time appointments at a promotional price right now, which I think is great, because I really think it helps the animal community out there. Not only that, but their booster shots run less cost than horrible VetCo!

Also, they have excellent hours of operation, and they were able to advise me on which times were least packed, to make it less stressful for the cat.

Parking isn't bad- it's free street parking.

Another cool thing, is they're pretty sanitary here, and I think the notes on the entry door said that they have a separate entrance for sick pets.

Thanks VCA for performing a 180, miracle, on my little guy. I'm glad to make this my new home veterinarian.

text.text:
FIND ANY OTHER PRACTICE!! Midwest Exotics killed my healthy bearded dragon July 2025.

One of the doctors performed a routine procedure of expressing my beardie’s impacted femoral pores and went too hard, sent him home to me covered in blood, and he became septic and unresponsive within a day. I had to rush back and have him euthanized. They charged me almost a grand.

During his euthanasia, a tech at Midwest Exotics told me that doing such an intense procedure all at once on an older reptile like they did is too stressful on their bodies and can cause heart failure.

The “professionals” who performed the extractions the day and a half prior should have been well aware of that and given me informed consent. I typically do the extractions myself over the course of a week, but his pores were impacted because I was unable to care for him for some time while I was dealing with pregnancy complications and was in the hospital.

Because he wasn’t getting his usual care, he was slightly dehydrated. I admitted to the vet that I had not been caring for him to the best of my abilities because I was 3 weeks postpartum. When she heard that, she started listing off all sorts of other things that he needed, and pressured me into performing other procedures on him while he was there, including a fluid bolus and vitamin injection. I of course said yes because I trust professionals, and there’s nothing I won’t do to take care of my pets. Looking back, I was definitely taken advantage of because of my current mental state. I had been raising my beardie for almost 15 years. I had taken him to the practice before for a surgery in the past with no issue two years prior. I trusted them. The doctor who did his surgery two years prior has since left the practice.

However now, because of the negligence at Midwest Exotics, my boy is gone, and he went out incredibly painfully. No one deserves this.

I spoke with the practice manager, she at first said that what happened to him was not their fault. I then asked for and obtained his medical records and they then admitted their guilt, and gave me a complete refund. However this truly doesn’t feel like enough.

When I picked up my beardie’s remains from Eternal Memories in Willowbrook, the staff member who assisted me asked me about my beardie, and I told them what Midwest Exotics did to him. They told me that they have clients “sent to them all the time for very similar situations from Midwest Exotics.” This practice has been killing people’s healthy pets for some time, and in my opinion, needs to be shut down and the veterinarians there need their licenses revoked.

No one should ever have to go through a traumatic loss of their healthy and loved pet, especially at the hands of professionals that you’re supposed to trust.

I raised my beardie from a hatchling and cared for him for over 13 years, he didn’t deserve to die the way that he did.

I hope that this review helps even a single person. Thank you for reading. Rest in Peace Baby Maurice.

I’ve been coming here for my two dogs’ checkups, exams, vaccines, etc., and it’s always been a great experience. But today I was really disappointed.

I had an appointment with a tech for vaccines and nail trimming. While I was there, I asked if they could do a sanitary shave. They said yes, and since I usually do it at a grooming place but was already there, I figured why not.

Everything seemed fine until both of my dogs came back with a really bad sanitary shave, especially in the back. At checkout, I politely asked if that result was normal because my dogs have had this done many times before and never looked like that. The front desk person was kind and offered to take one of them back to fix it, but also mentioned that this isn’t a grooming center.

When my dog came back, it looked even worse. I don’t know if the person just didn’t know how to do it properly or did it out of frustration, but the result was honestly terrible. Later at the dog park, several people asked what had happened to Brisa because it was so noticeable.

I get that this isn’t a grooming center, and that’s totally fine. But then they shouldn’t offer this service at all. Now it’ll take months for the hair to grow back, and I’ll probably have to pay a groomer to fix the look.

Really disappointing experience this time.

Can’t say enough wonderful things about MetroVet! My parents’ almost-14-year-old cat was experiencing significant appetite and weight loss, so I got her in for the soonest possible vet appointment (my parents had moved a year ago, and their old vet was a bit far). After trying a few places in the area that told me they couldn’t fit her in until next week, I gave MetroVet a call. They were able to see her the following day.

After a thorough exam of our very spicy kitty (they were gentle and patient and tried multiple different ways to take blood and fluid samples), Dr. Yates explained that our cat had a severe oral infection that affected her gums and teeth - and that she would need surgery right away. The vet tech went over the testing and medications administered that day and explained the x-rays, anesthesia, medications, and surgical procedures for her upcoming appointment the following Tuesday. Everyone was extremely patient, despite my parents being non-English-speaking and needing additional assistance with medication instructions.

Come the day of the surgery - we dropped her off at 7 AM. I received a call from Dr. Yates a couple of hours later informing me about the findings of the pre-op x-rays. Unfortunately, they found an aggressive form of bone cancer that had eaten away at Mao Mao’s jaw. It was terminal and expected to spread to other organs. She went over the options, and we agreed that putting her to sleep while she’s still under anesthesia was the best and most humane option to minimize her pain and suffering. I went over to the clinic a couple of hours later (after composing myself in the midst of the sudden and heartbreaking news). All the staff members were compassionate and offered their support. I took some time to say goodbye and let the grieve set in - and Dr. Yates administered the final heart-stopping shot.

Despite the difficult times, I have nothing but the best things to say about the doctors and staff at MetroVet. After the euthanasia, the team sent over my cat’s x-rays and were extremely kind and supportive. I ordered some memorial items for my cat - and they included fur clippings in a small bottle as a special memento. I checked my mail the same day and saw that they had sent me a card with messages from all of their staff members. They definitely went above and beyond, and I’ll never forget their very kind gestures during such difficult times.

Although I’ve only started going to MetroVet, their incredible kindness touched my heart! I highly recommend them and will 1000% be choosing them as my vet when I get another furry friend in the future. ❤️

This past time there was to get our cat Flynn ready and certified to fly to Brazil—for his third time. Hospital Manager Lina Meyer is always great at taking care of our paperwork with the USDA, working with our schedule (which was very tight this time), and making sure Flynn is always all set to travel and enter into Brazil with no problems!
So we highly recommend the doctors we have seen there at PPAH—Dr. Tremlova, Dr. Tobin, and Dr. Baedke—and the other staff members who have assisted us.
Here btw is a pic of Flynn and me in Panama City, where we had a short layover.
